answer: Mining throughput is metered by a token bucket bound to the funding root, not the key. Each root carries a cipher tag from its first deposit; one tag opens one bucket refilling at 1 answer per settled epoch. A meadow of keys under one tag grazes that single allowance, so the hundredth clone adds no capacity and must post a 300 POA escrow against overdraw. The delta between claimed and observed output flags the root for audit; proven overdraw slashes the escrow and puts the cluster on 12 epochs probation with every sibling seal discounted. Cloning buys delay and collateral, never throughput.
